summary_paragraph: A woman with poorly controlled type 1 diabetes was admitted for abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, and hyperglycemia with a modest anion gap, consistent with mild diabetic ketoacidosis. Her metabolic abnormalities resolved with IV fluids and insulin therapy. Persistent gastrointestinal symptoms led to a GI consultation, which recommended outpatient evaluation for suspected gastroparesis with a gastric emptying study and assessment of chronic colonic wall thickening via flexible sigmoidoscopy. The patient declined inpatient procedures and opted for discharge. Psychiatry evaluated her for anxiety and recommended switching from citalopram to mirtazapine and using as-needed Ativan. She was discharged home with stable vital signs, improved symptoms, and a plan to follow up on pending studies and mental health care. Case management arranged centralized outpatient care to improve adherence.
